note:
Although Serbs follow Vuk's rule "write as you speak", mistakes happen.

Written together instead of separately:
• «самном» instead of са мно̑м
• «неможу» instead of не мо̀гу
• «видеће те» instead of ви̏дећете

Common mistakes inside words:
• «сумљам» instead of сумњам - dissimilation
• «прекључе» instead of пре̏кјуче̄ - an inserted л
• «хвали» instead of фали - hypercorrection
• «предпоставља» instead of претпоставља
title: Spelling mistakes Serbs make

note:
The mistake «ми бих чули» instead of ми бисмо чули: the auxiliary verb changes by person.

Serbian dislikes two vowels in a row, so an extra «ј» appears: «авијон» instead of авѝо̄н.

«Требамо да» is a Croatianism; in Serbian you say требало би да.
title: More mistakes: ми бих, авијон

note:
In the Niš dialect the cases are gradually being lost under the influence of neighboring languages, and prepositions make the endings redundant.

So the instrumental and the locative are replaced by the accusative: «са књигу» instead of са књигом.
title: The Niš dialect: cases fade away

related.en: rich dough (enriched with eggs and butter)
plain unleavened dough (stretched, as for strudel)

note:
Serbian names of dough:
• дизано - yeast dough
• кисело - rich dough
• бѝсквӣт - sponge, biscuit
• ливено - batter, for pancakes
• лиснато - puff pastry

• прхко - shortcrust
• принцес маса - choux pastry, for eclairs
• и̏нтегра̄лно - wholegrain
• смрзнуто - frozen
title: Kinds of dough

note:
In Serbian ко̑т means a litter, a brood, and also a breed.

Hence окотити се - to give birth to young (of various animals, a panda among them).

A male cat is ма́чак, while ма̏чка came from Hungarian.
title: Кот and мачка

hinny (offspring of a stallion and a female donkey)

note:
Horse colors:
• вра́нац - black
• бе́лац, чѝла̄ш - white
• си́вац, зѐле̄нко - gray
• дорат - bay
• а̀ла̄т, риђан - chestnut
• кулаш - dun
• шарац - piebald

More words:
• ко̀била - mare, ждре̑бе - foal
• мула - mule (donkey and mare)

related.en: fight fire with fire (literally: a nail is driven out by a nail)

note:
Many Latin proverbs have Serbian counterparts:
• manus manum lavat - рука руку мије
• divide et impera - завади па владај
• clavus clavo - клин се клином избија
• per aspera ad astra - кроз тр̑ње до зве́зда
title: Latin sayings in Serbian

note:
In standard Serbian the stress moved one syllable forward in the 15th-16th centuries: рукА, ногА became рУка, нОга. Below, the stressed syllable is written with a capital letter.

In Old Shtokavian dialects, for example that of Kruševac, the stress stayed where it was before the shift:
• палАчинке, not палачИнке
• бАнана, not банАна
• нУтела, not нутЕла

This is a dialect, not the standard: nobody talks like that on TV.
title: Stress: Kruševac and the Neo-Shtokavian shift

note:
Пољопрѝвреда is divided into branches:
• воћарство - fruit growing
• рата́рство - field crops
• повртарство - vegetable growing
• сточа́рство - livestock

Земљора́дња is farming, and пољопри̏вредник and земљо̀ра̄днӣк both mean a farmer.

Бѐрба is the harvest, picking; the verb is бра̏ти.
title: Branches of agriculture

note:
Relief and geography:
• клѝсура - a gorge with gentle slopes
• лѝтица - with steep slopes
• окопина - grotto
• пѐћина - cave
• ма̏јдан - a small quarry or mine
• прераст - natural stone bridge
• сига - tufa
• слив реке - river basin
title: Relief and geography

note:
Хајдучка трава is yarrow, from ха̀јдӯк (an outlaw).

Посеко̀тина is St John's wort, and in everyday speech a cut: the word is used both for the herb and for the wound.

These are folk names, not scientific ones.
title: Names of plants: хајдучка трава and посекотина

note:
The root црп- means "to scoop, to draw (liquid)":
• цр̏псти, ѝсцр̄псти
• и̏сцрпан - exhaustive
• ѝсцрпљен - worn out
• исцр̀пљив, не̏исцр̄пан

Grouping words by root helps memory. The same goes for the root мор-: у́мор, о̀дмор, за̀моран.
title: Words with the root црп-

note:
Many different Serbian words where English has just "pipe" or "tube":
• ди̏мња̄к, о̀џак - chimney, flue
• лу̀ла - smoking pipe
• слу̏шалица - telephone receiver
• це̑в - water pipe
• цѐвчица - small tube
• сла̀мчица - drinking straw
• тру́ба - trumpet
• а̀успух - exhaust pipe
title: Serbian words for a pipe and a tube

note:
Beer is светло or тамно (light or dark), точено (draft); craft beer is занатско пиво.

Домаће пиво is beer produced locally, not homemade beer.

More words:
• пѝвара - brewery
• пи́вница - pub
• кри́гла - beer mug

What beer is made of: сла̑д (malt), хме̏љ (hops), ква́сац (yeast).
title: Beer: how people talk about it

note:
Пла̑в means a pale color in the range from yellow to blue, so пла̑ва ко̀са is fair hair. The name of the Polovtsians (Cumans) comes from the same root ("yellow").

Proto-Slavic tolt becomes tlat in Serbian:
• гла́ва - head
• мла̑д - young
• гла̑с - voice
• бла̏то - swamp
title: Плав and the Polovtsians; Serbian «tlat» words

note:
The speech of southern Kosovo and Metohija differs in these ways:
• the stress falls on other syllables: СрбИја, писАли. The stressed syllable is written with a capital letter
• there are almost no tones or lengths
• a simplified case system: the accusative merged with the locative - студирао у Београд instead of студирао у Београду

This is not a mistake, but foreigners are advised to learn the standard.
title: The Kosovo dialect: how it differs

note:
Stages of the school system:
• вр̀тић - kindergarten
• нулто одељење - the preparatory year (grade zero)
• основна школа - 8 years, lower and upper grades
• средња школа - secondary: гѝмна̄зија (academic) or стручна школа (vocational)

The year is divided into полугодишта (half-years) or тромесечја (terms). A break is ра́спуст, winter (зимски) or summer (летњи).
title: The school system of Serbia

note:
Foreign words in Serbian sometimes have a gender you would not guess:
• мо̑ј про̀грам, мо̑ј про̀бле̄м - masculine
• мо̀ја су̏па, мо̀ја адрѐса - feminine

The constitution is usually called у̏ста̄в, and еконо̀мија is the economy.
title: Gender of loanwords

note:
Serbian has no ü sound, so French ü is written with и:
• пи̏ре, жѝрӣ, мѐнӣ, би̏ро
• нија̀нса
• Цирих, Брѝсел, Мѝнхен
• Кири

Surrealism is надреалѝзам. Brochure stays брошура, not «брошира».
title: French ü and Serbian и

note:
Nicknames in «-и» (Зоки, Боки, Паки, Мики, Ла̏кӣ) are declined, and a «ј» is inserted between «и» and the ending:
• од Пакија
• дајем Пакију
• са Пакијем
• воли Пакија
• о Пакију
• vocative - Паки!

Not declined: foreign words ending in two vowels (кака̏о), some colors and Chinese names.
title: Pet names in «-и» are declined

note:
Adjectives that have no exact English equivalent:
• па̏метан - smart, and also "knowledgeable"
• зго̏дан - with a nice figure
• опу̏штен - relaxed, at ease
• по̏штова̄нӣ - respected, "dear"; you can address people this way even without a name, it is not rude
• насмѐјан - smiling, cheerful
• ша̏шав - eccentric, quirky
• за̀послен - employed
• фи̑н - nice, decent
• ки̏лав - sluggish, limp

Separately: же́дан сам - "I'm thirsty".
title: Adjectives with no exact English equivalent

note:
In Serbian, feminine forms of job titles are standard:
• лѐкарка, фри̏зерка
• мѝниста̄рка, дѝректорка
• научница

But адво̀ка̄т, инжѐње̄р, прево̀дилац, во̀за̄ч, тре́нер are traditionally masculine.

Forms such as боркиња, фотографкиња, политикологиња are considered non-standard by the language academy.
title: Feminine job titles in Serbian

note:
The suffix -арина forms names of a fee or tax:
• путарѝна - road toll
• мостарина - bridge toll
• стана̀рина - rent
• школа̀рина - tuition
• члана̀рина - membership fee

Obsolete: трошарина (excise tax), крчмарина, сплаварина, свадбарина.

The stress falls on -ин-: путарИна.
title: The suffix -арина: a fee for something

note:
Serbs write foreign names as they are pronounced: По̑л (Paul), И́го (Hugo). Croats, on the contrary, keep the original.

Another trend: words like online, wi-fi and job titles stay in English, in the Latin alphabet.
title: Serbianization and Latinization of foreign names

note:
The vocative does not express a relation between words, so it has no single ending:
• feminine words more often take -о (кафано)
• sometimes it coincides with the nominative
• forms differ by region
title: The vocative in Serbian

note:
Пѐрфект is the ordinary past tense.

Two other forms are rarer:
• the aorist (from perfective verbs: ја̑ рѐкох) - an emotional retelling of quick events, or a bookish style
• the imperfect (from imperfective verbs: ја̑ бе̏х) - narration of events long ago

In speech you only need the perfect; it is enough to recognize the others when you read fairy tales.
title: Aorist and imperfect: the fairy-tale tenses

note:
The suffix -ина forms nouns of size from adjectives:
• ду̏г - дужѝна
• шѝрок - ширѝна
• дѐбео - дебљѝна
• гу̑ст - густѝна
• вѝсок - висѝна
• ду̀бок - дубѝна
• те́жак - тежѝна

Watch the alternation in the root: д > ж (дужѝна), ео > љ (дебљѝна).

All these words are feminine, and the question is always «колика је...?» (how big is...?).
title: The suffix -ина: names of sizes and measures

note:
In 2021 the Law on Gender Equality came into force in Serbia, and a guide to "родно осетљив језик" (gender-sensitive language) was issued with it.

Here the word ро̑д means social gender, and по̑л means biological sex.

The guide recommends:
• naming both groups: дру̏гови и дру̑гарице, студенти и студенткиње
• using feminine forms of job titles

The idea caused controversy: critics find such forms clumsy.
title: Gender-sensitive language

note:
In Serbia a residence permit is processed at the полицијска управа (police department). Temporary residence is called прѝвременӣ бо̀равак.

The grounds are given with по основу:
• школовања - studies
• спајања породице - family reunification
• лечења - medical treatment
• власништва над непокретношћу - ownership of real estate

Бе̑лӣ ка̀рто̄н is a certificate of registration of a foreigner at the place of stay.
title: Words for residence permit paperwork

note:
Many words are built from the root клиз- ("to slide"):
• кли̏зав (slippery), кли́зити (to slide)
• кли̏зӣште (landslide)
• клѝзалӣште (skating rink)
• клѝзаљке (ice skates)
• клѝза̄ч (skater)
• уметничко клизање (figure skating)

Sliding doors and sliding wardrobes also "slide": клизна врата, клизни орман.
title: The root клиз-: to slide

note:
Sea fish: орада (bream), бранцин (sea bass), ту̏на, ха̀рӣнга (herring), бака̀ла̄р (cod), о̏слић (hake).

River fish: ша̀ран (carp), гр̀ге̄ч (perch), сму̑ђ (pikeperch), со̏м (catfish).

Seafood is мо̀рскӣ пло̀дови or пло̀дови мо̏ра:
• ли̏гње (squid), шкољке (clams), да̏гње (mussels)
• ко̀зице (shrimp), о̏стрига (oyster)

related.en: the first guest on Christmas Day
to visit, to come to see

note:
Christmas Eve in Serbian is Ба̑дњи да̑н. The word is linked to the verb "to keep vigil", and there is also a folk legend about a god Badnya.

On this day people burn the ба̏дња̄к - oak branches.

Че̏сница is a ritual loaf that is broken by hand (hence ча̑ст, a share).

По̀ложајник is the first guest on Christmas Day; he brings luck to the house. The word is formed from по̀лазити.
title: Serbian Christmas words

note:
Operations:
• са̀бира̄ње (+)
• о̀дузима̄ње (-)
• мно̏же̄ње (x)
• де̏ље̄ње (:)

How examples are read:
• 1 + 3 = 4 - један плус три једнако је четири
• 5 - 2 = 3 - пет минус два једнако је три
• 5 x 2 = 10 - пет пута два једнако је десет
• 20 : 2 = 10 - двадесет подељено са два једнако је десет

Division can be са остатком or без остатка (with or without a remainder).
title: Arithmetic: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division

Listings for apartments for sale say:
• ко̀мплетно реновѝра̄ње - complete renovation
• де̏лимично реновѝра̄ње - partial
• козметички радови - cosmetic

The phrase стан је у изворном стању means the apartment has not been renovated since it was built and is in its original condition.
title: Apartment renovation in listings

related.en: proof of payment of the fee

note:
Who is who:
• legal entity - пра̑вно ли́це
• entrepreneur (sole proprietor) - предузѐтник
• LLC - друштво са ограниченом одговорношћу (ДОО)

How to register a company with the Агенција за привредне регистре (АПР):
1. Submit a пријава.
2. State the назив фирме and the ши̏фра дела́тности.
3. Attach the доказ о плаћеној такси.

The tax regime is паушално опорезивање (flat-rate taxation). VAT is ПДВ (порез на додату вредност).

note:
Body types:
• лимузи́на - sedan
• хе̏чбек
• кара̀ва̄н - station wagon
• терѐнац or џи̏п - SUV
• ко̏мби - minibus, van

Drive: пре̑дњӣ, за̏дњӣ or на чѐтири то̏чка (front, rear or four-wheel).

Year of manufacture is го̀диште. Mileage is described with the verb пре̑ћи: «Прешао је сто хиљада километара».

note:
For inhabitants of countries Serbian has separate masculine and feminine words:
• Ср̏бин - Ср̏пкиња
• Ру̏с - Ру̏скиња
• Ѐнгле̄з - Ѐнглескиња
• Хр̀ва̄т - Хрватица
• Не́мац - Нѐмица
• Алба́нац - А̀лба̄нка
• Црно̀горац - Црно̀го̄рка

In the plural the masculine form is used: Срби, Ру̏си, Алба́нци.

The language is named with an adjective: ср̏пскӣ, ру̏скӣ, нѐмачкӣ, ѐнгле̄скӣ.
title: Inhabitants of countries: Србин - Српкиња

Love in the Time of Cholera (Márquez)

Russian classics are translated into Serbian close to the original, but some titles differ:

Meat is named from the animal with the suffix -етина:
• сви́ња - свѝњетина (pork)

• тѐле - тѐлетина (veal)

note:
Masculine job titles are formed with suffixes:
• -ац - пи́сац, про̀да̄вац
• -лац - слу̀шалац, глѐдалац
• -ар - ме̏са̄р, ри̏ба̄р
• -ач - во̀за̄ч, пѐва̄ч
• -ник - ра̑днӣк
• -ист(а) - економиста
• -аш - коша̀рка̄ш
• -ер - фудба̀ле̄р
• -тељ - у̀читељ, во̀дитељ
• -џија - ћевапџија, a Turkish suffix for trades

Which suffix to choose cannot be derived by a rule: it simply developed that way in the language.
title: Suffixes of job titles

note:
Feminine forms are made like this:
• -ац, -ач, -аш > -ица: продава̀чица, воза̀чица, кошарка̀шица
• -ар, -ер > -ка: месарка, тенисерка
• -ник > -ица: радница
• -ист(а) > -киња: економисткиња
• -тељ > -ка or -ица: водитељка, учитѐљица
• -џија > -ка

Inhabitants:
• Бео̀грађанин - Бео̀грађа̄нка
• Црно̀горац - Црно̀го̄рка
• Сара̀јлија - Са̀ра̄јка
• Не́мац - Нѐмица
• Ру̏с - Ру̏скиња
title: Feminine forms of job titles and of inhabitants

related.en: The green vegetables were not tasty.

note:
Words in -је denote many objects, but grammatically they are neuter singular:
• ка̀ме̄ње, ли̑шће, пе̑рје
• во̀ће, по̀врће
• др̀ве̄ће, цве̑ће

The verb is singular, and the adjective is neuter:
• Моје цвеће је свеже.
• Зелено поврће није било укусно.
• Дрвеће је већ жуто.
title: Collective nouns in -је

note:
Abstract nouns are formed with suffixes:
• -ота - лепо̀та, срамо̀та
• -ина - топлѝна, величѝна
• -ило - лу̀дило
• -ај - по̏куша̄ј, о̏прошта̄ј, за̏грља̄ј
• -ба - сва̀дба, вѐридба, бо̀рба
• -ња - ше́тња, па̀тња, пре́тња
• -ње - чѝта̄ње, образова́ње
• -ство - пријатѐљство
• -ост - ста̏ро̄ст, хра́бро̄ст, захва́лно̄ст

Words in -ост are always feminine.
title: Suffixes of abstract nouns

note:
Besides the usual surnames in -ић, Bosnia has nickname surnames. People took them under Austria-Hungary, when everyone was required to have a surname.

Many mean everyday words or traits:
• Врачар - healer
• Шѐгрт - apprentice
• Дроњак - ragamuffin
• Ђога - oaf
• Ждеро - glutton
• Га̏ће - underpants
• Копривица - little nettle
title: Meaningful Bosnian surnames

note:
The neutral word is но̀вац. Cash is ке̏ш, готовѝна.

Па̏ре is colloquial, but acceptable everywhere except in documents.

Slang:
• ло́ва, ки̑нта, ди̏нџа
• шушке - paper money
• зеленбаћ - greenbacks, dollars
• денге - borrowed from Russian

Sums:
• ба̀нка - a tenner
• со̏м - a grand
• кило, ци́гла - a million
title: Money in Serbian: from standard to slang

note:
According to the Ethnographic Museum, black stands for night, death and danger, but also for modesty, melancholy and rebellion (rock culture).

Hence the expressions:
• црна овца - black sheep
• црне мисли - dark thoughts
• цр̑нӣ ху̀мор - black humor
• црна листа - blacklist
• црна рупа - black hole
title: What «црни» (black) means in Serbian culture

note:
Names of fairy-tale characters in Serbian:
• Ру̑жно па̏че - The Ugly Duckling
• Пепѐљуга - Cinderella
• Снежана - Snow White
• Мала сирена - The Little Mermaid
• Палчица - Thumbelina
• Снежна краљица - The Snow Queen
• Принцеза на зрну грашка - The Princess and the Pea

In Serbia only children's cartoons are dubbed; films for adults are shown with subtitles.
title: Names of fairy-tale characters in Serbian

note:
The boy Пѐрица is the Serbian counterpart of Little Johnny. His jokes can be childish or rude, but in children's collections they are simple and suitable for beginner reading.

A typical pun: in an English lesson Перица calls the rooms ливингрум, батрум, по̀друм, because по̀друм (basement) also ends in "-rum", like "room".
title: Перица - the hero of Serbian jokes

note:
In a Serbian film in a southern dialect you can hear:
• the stress does not move forward (готово, ПАцови; the stressed syllable is written with a capital letter)
• few cases: ти си у ту секту instead of ти си у то̑ј се̑ктӣ
• other words: убаво (beautiful), збо̀рити (to speak), шта работиш

The future tense: ће comes first, without да: ће ви̏дӣш, ће се видимо.

A dialect in Serbia is normal and not stigmatized.
title: The southern dialect in films

related.en: to hate on someone, to troll

note:
Serbian spelling is phonetic, so English words are written as they sound:
• фјучерс (futures)
• хепиенд (happy end)
• хе̏јтовати (to hate)
• серчовати (to search)
• даунлоудовати (to download)

Adapting a foreign word to Serbian is called посрбљавање. There is a dictionary of new anglicisms with about 4,500 words.
title: Anglicisms are written as they sound

note:
Slang loves exaggeration and comparisons with objects:
• вугла - head; the syllables are swapped from гла́ва, which is how ша̏тровачкӣ го̏во̄р works
• њу̏шка, фа̑ца - mug, face
• радари - ears (radars)
• ка̏нџе - nails (claws)
• ви̏ле - hands (pitchforks)
• фарови - eyes (headlights)
• кљу̑н - beak (nose or mouth)
• чука - heart
• гиљарке - legs

Much of it sounds rude or jokey.
title: Body parts in slang

note:
Word-for-word translation leads to mistakes:
• де̏сити се takes the dative: шта му се десило - what happened to him
• лепа идеја simply means «a good idea»
• in speech где (where) is often used instead of куда (where to): где идеш? for куда идеш?

Which case a verb takes has to be learned for each verb.
title: Traps of word-for-word translation

note:
Space in Serbian:
• Ме̏се̄ц - the Moon
• све̏мӣр - the universe
• помра̀че̄ње - eclipse
• сазвѐжђе - constellation
• небеско тело - celestial body
• Сунчев систем - the Solar System
• ва̏здӯшнӣ омо̀та̄ч - atmosphere
• Вѐликӣ Мѐдвед and Ма̑лӣ Мѐдвед - the Big and Little Dipper (Ursa Major and Minor)
• Севе́рњача - Polaris, the North Star
• месечеве мене - phases of the Moon
title: Space in Serbian

note:
Children go to вр̀тић, then to основна школа (8 years), then to средња школа: a gymnasium or a vocational school (стручна школа).

There is no separate primary school: people say нижи разреди основне школе (the lower grades).

The school-leaving exam is мату́ра, and a graduate is ма̀турант.

Schools are often named after writers and scholars, for example "Вук Караџић".
title: The school system of Serbia

note:
Serbia has no single "service center": services are provided by individual craftsmen in kiosks around the city:
• shoes are repaired by an о̀бућа̄р
• keys are copied by a кључар or бра̏ва̄р
• watches are repaired by a ча̀со̄внича̄р
• jewelry - зла̀та̄р
• clothes are altered by a кро̀ја̄ч
• fur - кр̀зна̄р
• knives are sharpened by an о̏штрач

Thread and needles are sold at a позамантерија (haberdashery).
title: Craftsmen instead of a one-stop service center

note:
In autumn people in Serbia put up зимница for the winter.

Spreads:
• а̀јва̄р, made of roasted peppers, is the king of spreads: бла̑гӣ (mild) or љу̑тӣ (hot)
• пѝнђур - eggplant spread
• љутѐница - hot pepper relish

Vegetables are pickled: ту̀ршија, кисели краставци, ки̏селӣ ку̀пус.

Sweets: сла̀тко̄ (fruit preserves, for example од ви̏ша̄ња̄), пѐкмез, мармела́да.
title: Зимница - preserves for the winter
